Bromsgrove's population increased by around 5,500 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 99,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Bromsgrove increased by 5.9%, from just over 93,600 in 2011 to around 99,200 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), but by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Bromsgrove was home to around 3.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.1 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 40% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Bromsgrove to the West Midlands as a whole

Median age in Bromsgrove

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Bromsgrove increased by one year, from 44 to 45 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 1,800 (an increase of 9.4%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just over 2,300 (11.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 0.7 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Bromsgrove stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Bromsgrove, but fell across the West Midlands.

In Bromsgrove, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 10.0% in 2011 to 10.7% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 19.0% to 18.2%.

Private renting in Bromsgrove increased from 8.8% to 10.6%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 79.5% to 77.5%.

The rate of social renting in Bromsgrove increased by 0.7 percentage points

Unemployment in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 2.1% of Bromsgrove residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were unemployed. This figure decreased from 2.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 6 in 10 people (57.2%) said they were employed (excluding full-time students), compared with 58.6% in 2011. The percentage of retired Bromsgrove residents increased from 25.4% to 27.1%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed was greater across the West Midlands (1.4 percentage points, from 4.6% to 3.2%) than in Bromsgrove (0.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 1.1 percentage points, from 4.0% to 2.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Bromsgrove decreased by 0.6 percentage points

Working hours in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 10.1% of Bromsgrove residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (10.2%).

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week increased from 9.6% to 9.9% across the West Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Bromsgrove decreased by 0.1 percentage points

Bromsgrove residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 92,200 Bromsgrove residents said they were born in England. This represented 93.0% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 87,500 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.5% of Bromsgrove's population.

Wales was the next most represented, with around 1,100 Bromsgrove residents reporting this country of birth (1.2%). This figure was down from just under 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.4% of the population of Bromsgrove.

The number of Bromsgrove residents born in Scotland fell from around 850 in 2011 (0.9% of the local population) to around 750 in 2021 (0.8%).

In 2021, 93.0% of Bromsgrove residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Bromsgrove

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the West Midlands (2.5 percentage points) than in Bromsgrove (0.4 percentage points).

In Bromsgrove, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity stayed close to 2.3% between the last two censuses. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 6.2% to 8.7%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Bromsgrove increased from 0.4% to 1.0%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 14.7% to 58.1%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Bromsgrove increased by 0.4 percentage points

Unpaid care in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 5.3% of Bromsgrove residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.5% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.4% in 2011. The proportion of Bromsgrove residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.3% to 2.4%.

This area had the region’s joint second highest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (alongside South Staffordshire). Across the region, only Staffordshire Moorlands, with 5.5%, had a higher proportion.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Bromsgrove decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Religion in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 37.4% of Bromsgrove residents reported having "No religion", up from 22.0% in 2011. The rise of 15.4 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Bromsgrove. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 53.5% of people in Bromsgrove described themselves as Christian (down from 68.9%), while 5.6% did not state their religion (down from 6.9% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 37.4% of usual residents in Bromsgrove reported having "No religion"

Disability in Bromsgrove

The increase in the age-standardised proportion of non-disabled residents was greater in nearby Birmingham (3.5 percentage points) than in Bromsgrove (1.1 percentage points).

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In Bromsgrove, the proportion of non-disabled residents increased from 83.3% in 2011 to 84.4% in 2021. During the same period, the proportion in nearby Birmingham increased from 76.6% to 80.1%.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Bromsgrove fell from 7.6% to 6.1%, while the percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a little increased from 9.1% to 9.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of non-disabled residents in Bromsgrove increased by 1.1 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 3.2% of Bromsgrove residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 2.1% in 2011. The 1.1 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 10.8% to 13.3%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 93.1% of people in Bromsgrove identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 95.8% in 2011), while 2.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.5% in 2011 to 0.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 3.2% of usual residents in Bromsgrove identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Fewer couples without children

Of Bromsgrove households, 17.7% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.1%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.0% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 7.5% to 7.6%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Bromsgrove (1.9 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (1.0 percentage points, from 16.9% to 15.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Bromsgrove decreased by 1.9 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Bromsgrove residents aged 16 years and over, 30.0% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 26.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (51.8%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 54.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Bromsgrove that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.6% to 9.0%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Bromsgrove (3.1 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the West Midlands (3.4 percentage points, from 33.7% to 37.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Bromsgrove increased by 3.1 percentage points

Health in Bromsgrove

In 2021, 52.2% of Bromsgrove residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 50.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 33.2% to 32.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Bromsgrove residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.9% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.5% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Bromsgrove increased by 2.2 percentage points
